intro: A horn call, a quiet trombone chorale and a great C-major string tune transform the First Symphony’s finale. Brahms saves the chorale for the final pages, where brass and strings proclaim it together.

sections.label: Intro · C minor and plucked strings
sections.mNote: Slow phrases alternate with pizzicato figures that accelerate

sections.label: B · The horn call in C major
sections.mNote: Horn and flute above muted string tremolo

sections.label: C · Trombones sing a chorale
sections.mNote: Bassoons support the brass; the horn call follows again

sections.label: A · The broad C-major violin tune
sections.mNote: Low strings pluck beneath the Allegro melody

sections.label: A′ · The tune returns and wanders
sections.mNote: C major leads out towards E♭ and F♯

sections.label: D · The descending bass comes home
sections.mNote: Winds and low strings exchange the four-note descent

sections.label: Coda · Faster strings and the great chorale
sections.mNote: A quiet buildup leads to Più allegro and C major

cues.title: Four notes falling
cues.text: Violas, cellos and double basses begin a four-note descent. Above them, the violins unfold a slow, troubled version of the melody that will later become the great C-major tune. For now it lives in C minor, interrupted by accelerating plucked strings.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 1–11, Simrock first edition (1877), p. 43 onwards; Kelly Dean Hansen’s score guide, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A horn above the tremolo
cues.text: C major opens under a horn call. Muted violins and violas tremble beneath the long notes, and the timpani roll softly. The tune passes between horns so it can keep singing without a break for breath; flutes take it up next.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, Più andante, bars 30–46; horn and flute statements, muted tremolo strings and timpani. Hansen, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A birthday tune for Clara
cues.text: In 1868 Brahms sends Clara Schumann a birthday greeting containing the melody that becomes this horn call. Eight years later, the private tune stands at the turning point of his First Symphony.
cues.evidence: Marc Mandel identifies the horn call as a birthday greeting to Clara Schumann from 1868. https://www.bso.org/works/symphony-no-1-in-c-minor

cues.title: The quiet trombone chorale
cues.text: Trombones and bassoons sing a short chorale. The trombones have waited until this movement to play at all. Their little hymn will stay out of sight through the Allegro, returning with the full orchestra near the end.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 47–51 and 407–416; Hansen’s score guide. The trombones’ restriction to the finale is also noted by Mandel. http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html; https://www.bso.org/works/symphony-no-1-in-c-minor
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The violins’ great tune
cues.text: Low in their range, the violins begin the broad C-major tune over plucked lower strings. Horns fill out the harmony. The phrase takes seventeen bars: its second half delays the cadence by one bar, giving the melody another breath.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, Allegro non troppo, ma con brio, bars 62–78; seventeen-bar melody and scoring described by Hansen. http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The tune ventures out again
cues.text: The broad tune returns in C major with a fuller accompaniment. Its continuation soon turns towards E♭ and then F♯. The violins have brought back a familiar melody and immediately found it new places to go.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 186–219; combined return and development. Hansen, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The horn call, changed
cues.text: The horn call returns, now with smoothly moving violas and cellos beneath it. The introduction’s trembling strings have gone. Violins extend the tune, then descend as Brahms marks calando — dying away.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 289–300; horn-call return and altered accompaniment. Hansen, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Four descending notes come home
cues.text: The second theme returns in C major. Its four-note descending bass passes between low strings and flute, clarinet and bassoon. The little descent from the finale’s first bars now has a whole family of voices.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 301–325; alternating wind and string statements of the descending ostinato. Hansen, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Low brass recall the opening
cues.text: Trombone, contrabassoon and low strings recall the main tune in its darker form. Violin arpeggios climb above a timpani roll. The phrases shorten and accelerate until seven hammered chords launch Più allegro.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, transition to coda, bars 367–390; Hansen’s score guide. http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The chorale fills the orchestra
cues.text: The quiet chorale returns in brass and strings together. It has waited since the introduction for this moment. Around it, the strings’ turning figures keep the faster coda moving towards the final C-major chords.
cues.evidence: First Symphony, IV, coda, bars 407–457; chorale reprise and C-major close. Hansen, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: C major opens under the horn
transitions.from: Intro · C minor and plucked strings
transitions.to: B · The horn call in C major
transitions.how: The surging C-minor introduction breaks off. Low strings descend and diminish into Più andante; the horn call opens in C major over a soft timpani roll and the trombones’ first entry. Muted violins and violas begin their tremolo beneath the tune.
transitions.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 24–38; Hansen’s score guide and Simrock first edition, p. 48. http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html

transitions.title: The flute leaves the trombones speaking
transitions.from: B · The horn call in C major
transitions.how: The flutes finish the C-major horn melody. Trombones and bassoons answer with a compact chorale in measured chords; a timpani roll marks its final downward leap. Horns then resume the call above string tremolo, building towards the dominant chord that prepares the Allegro.
transitions.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 38–61; Hansen’s score guide, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.

transitions.title: Held brass release the violin tune
transitions.to: A · The broad C-major violin tune
transitions.how: Horn and trombone hold the dominant chord on G as the other instruments fall silent. Violins emerge low in their range with the broad C-major melody, supported by horns and plucked cellos and basses. The marking is Allegro non troppo, ma con brio.
transitions.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 52–78; Hansen’s score guide and Simrock first edition, p. 52. http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html

transitions.title: Quiet winds lead the tune home
transitions.from: A · The broad C-major violin tune
transitions.to: A′ · The tune returns and wanders
transitions.how: After the closing E-minor cadence, quiet rising wind figures lead back to the broad violin tune in C major. Its accompaniment is fuller now. The continuation turns towards E♭ and F♯, taking the returned melody into another long development.
transitions.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 176–219; Hansen’s score guide, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.

transitions.title: The horn call yields to descending basses
transitions.from: A′ · The tune returns and wanders
transitions.to: D · The descending bass comes home
transitions.how: The returning horn call broadens over moving strings. Violins extend it, then descend under pulsating timpani, marked calando. All strings introduce the second group’s four-note descent in C major; subsequent statements alternate between low strings and flute, clarinet and bassoon.
transitions.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 289–315; Hansen’s score guide, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.

transitions.title: Quiet fragments gather over tremolo
transitions.from: D · The descending bass comes home
transitions.to: Coda · Faster strings and the great chorale
transitions.how: The C-minor closing cadence subsides into quiet rising figures from horns, violins and clarinets over viola tremolo. Trombone, contrabassoon and low strings recall the main tune above a long timpani roll. Violin arpeggios shorten and climb; stringendo drives the passage towards the faster C-major coda.
transitions.evidence: First Symphony, IV, bars 360–391; Hansen’s score guide, http://www.kellydeanhansen.com/opus68.html.

source.title: Brahms, Symphony No. 1, Simrock first-edition full score, plate 7957 (1877)
source.locator: IV. Adagio — Più andante — Allegro, pp. 43–100; horn call at bar 30, chorale at bar 47, Allegro at bar 62 and later returns. Bar references follow Kelly Dean Hansen’s score guide.

timeline.note: Low strings descend four notes beneath a slow violin version of the coming Allegro tune.
All-string pizzicato figures pass between registers in the first accelerating interruption.
The Più andante introduces the horn call over quiet brass support, timpani and muted string tremolo.
Flutes take up the horn call above string tremolo, with a trumpet echo.
Trombones and bassoons sing the short chorale, with contrabassoon and low horn support.
The broad Allegro tune begins in strings over plucked lower strings and supporting horns.
Winds and violins exchange fragments of the broad tune as more brass join.
The second group sets its melodic line above the recurring four-note bass descent.
The broad violin tune returns in C major, supported by horns and answering winds.
The horn call returns above smoothly moving violas and cellos.
Low strings and winds exchange the four-note descending bass in C major.
Low brass and strings recall the main tune beneath rising violin arpeggios and a timpani roll.
Brass and strings proclaim the chorale together in the faster C-major coda.

composer.epithet: He kept his First Symphony waiting until he was forty-three, then began the Second beside an Austrian lake the next summer.
facts: Piano with Otto Cossel; piano and composition with Eduard Marxsen in Hamburg
Detmold, 1857–59 · Vienna Singakademie, 1863–64 · Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde, 1872–75
Vienna; summers in Baden-Baden, Pörtschach, Mürzzuschlag and Bad Ischl

composer.background:
In the autumn of 1853, a twenty-year-old pianist from Hamburg arrived at the Schumanns’ home in Düsseldorf with an introduction from Joseph Joachim. Johannes Brahms played his own music. Robert Schumann heard a composer of the future and announced him that October in an article called Neue Bahnen — New Paths. Publishers became interested. Brahms now had to live up to a public prophecy before most of the public had heard a note. The young man’s piano sonatas were enormous; the symphonies Schumann expected would take much longer.

Brahms’s father Johann Jakob earned his living playing instruments including the horn and double bass. His mother, Christiane Nissen, was a seamstress. Born in Hamburg in 1833, he studied piano with Otto Cossel and then piano and composition with Eduard Marxsen, who grounded him in Bach, Mozart and Beethoven. He played, arranged and accompanied for money. A tour with the Hungarian violinist Ede Reményi in 1853 brought him to Joachim, and Joachim sent him on to Düsseldorf.
